# Research: wheels with maximum friction coefficient for Rescue Line

> **Date:** 2026-07-03  
> **Context:** the robot loses traction on the ramp (see [2026-07-02-independent-audit-ramp-silver.md](2026-07-02-independent-audit-ramp-silver.md)). An investigation was conducted to determine which wheel material maximizes grip for a robot weighing ~1–2 kg on RCJ track (white painted MDF/laminate, 25° ramps, silver/aluminum surfaces, dusty environment), both in commercial wheels and in moldable compounds.  
> **Methodology:** deep multi-agent research (21 sources, 25 claims subjected to adversarial verification with 3 votes: 22 confirmed, 3 refuted). Each claim in this document carries its confidence level. **No μ cited was measured on the actual RCJ surfaces** — bench validation is mandatory before deciding (golden rule 3 of the repo).  
> **Update 2026-07-03 (2nd pass):** an external analysis (ChatGPT) on the same topic was contrasted. New ideas were incorporated **only after verifying them against primary sources** (actual datasheets, manufacturer pages); what did not survive verification was marked. Details at the end in "Contrast with external analysis".  
> **Regulatory restriction:** the [official Rescue Line 2026 rules](https://rescue.rcj.cloud/rules/2026/RCJRescueLine2026-final.pdf) prohibit damaging the field — discard any solution that leaves residue, tears tape, or marks the track. Every candidate wheel must pass the criterion "roll on clean paper without leaving a mark".

---

## 1. Physics first: why "the stickiest material" is the wrong question

**Confidence: HIGH** — verified 3-0 against peer-reviewed papers (Persson & Xu, *J. Chem. Phys.* 163, 141001, 2025; Tiwari et al., *Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering*, 2020; *Tribology Letters* 73:106, 2025).

1. **The friction of an elastomer has two mechanisms**, not one:
   - **Adhesion**: shearing in the **real contact area** between rubber and floor (stick-slip events of polymer segments at the nanometric scale).
   - **Viscoelastic hysteresis**: energy dissipated when cyclically deforming against the substrate's roughness.

   On **smooth** surfaces (painted MDF, laminate, aluminum ramp), the adhesive term dominates, and what maximizes it is the **real contact area**.

2. **The real contact area is maximized by low modulus (low Shore A hardness), not "stickiness."** Key experiment (Tiwari et al. 2020): silanizing glass reduces the adhesion work **by half** and the rubber friction coefficient **barely changes**. Verbatim quote: *"There is no simple relation between adhesion and friction."* A material that feels sticky to the touch does not necessarily grip more.

3. **Low hardness = more friction on clean smooth floor** (measured): on clean epoxy, NBR of 57.9 Shore A gave COF 2.216 vs 0.70 with 84 Shore A (p<0.0001), due to reduced real contact area. *Caveat: the study covers 57.9–84 ShA; extrapolation to 10–30A is directional, not measured.*

4. **Counterintuitive and key for RCJ — low hardness also wins with dust** (*Tribology Letters* 2025): on smooth floors contaminated with particles, **softer** rubbers gave **higher** COF (p<0.0001), because in that condition, the particle-floor interaction (rolling of particles) dominates, and the soft rubber suppresses it. The real cost of the soft and knobby compound is **operational** (it needs to be cleaned before each run), not mechanical.

5. **The target number:** to climb 25° you need μ > tan(25°) ≈ **0.47**, plus margin for weight transfer and acceleration → aim for **effective μ ≥ 0.8–1.0**. Easily achievable with PU/silicone Shore A 10–30.

6. **The sweet spot is Shore A 15–30, not "the softest available."** Below ~10A, the wheel excessively deforms under load, wears out quickly, and picks up track dust without real grip gain. The casting guides for sumo wheels (miscircuitos.com, mcuoneclipse.com) agree: *"the rubber needs Shore A between 20 or 30."*

**About photocopier rollers** (initial hypothesis of the team): the instinct is correct — they are exactly this, industrial silicones/urethanes of low Shore A. But they are not "the best available": they are the industrial version of what can be bought or molded adapted to our wheel.

## 2. The 10 solutions, ranked

### Verified with sources (confidence HIGH/MEDIUM)

#### 1. FingerTech polyurethane wheels Shore A20 — best commercial option found

- **What it is:** PU Shore A20 tire degassed under vacuum on anodized aluminum 6061 rim. Grip standard in mini-sumo. There is a Shore A45 variant (more durable, less grip).
- **μ declared by the manufacturer:** **1.75 against unpainted smooth MDF** (vs 1.30 silicone and 1.05 rubber in their own test). *Caveat verified 2-1: benchmark from the manufacturer itself, with no published methodology, on unpainted MDF — do not assume it transfers to white painted MDF or the silver ramp.*
- **Diameters:** 44.45 / 50.8 (48.5 g) / 63.5 / 76.2 mm — three fall within the 30–70 mm range.
- **Observed price:** mini-sumo 1.125" ≈ USD 16.79 per pair; sumo line ≈ CAD 23.87.
- **Purchase:** [FingerTech mini-sumo wheels](https://www.fingertechrobotics.com/proddetail.php?prod=ft-minisumo-wheels-1125) · [FingerTech sumo wheels](https://www.fingertechrobotics.com/proddetail.php?prod=ft-sumo-wheel) — import from Canada or via RobotShop. Import cost and time to Argentina: **not established, quote**.
- **Mandatory maintenance** (required by the manufacturer, verified 3-0): *"Clean the tires with isopropyl alcohol wipes before each match for optimal traction."*

#### 2. Molding with Smooth-On VytaFlex 20 (urethane Shore 20A) — best homemade option

- **What it is:** urethane rubber of the same family and nominal hardness as the FingerTech compound.
- **Why it is viable for a school team** (datasheet verified 3-0): mix **1A:1B by volume or weight**, **does not require vacuum degassing**, negligible shrinkage. 3D printed mold + petroleum jelly as a release agent, curing ~16–24 h.
- **Independent corroboration of use in sumo wheels:** [miscircuitos.com](https://miscircuitos.com/how-to-cast-sumo-wheels-handmade/) · [mcuoneclipse.com](https://mcuoneclipse.com/2017/12/28/making-perfect-sticky-diy-sumo-robot-tires/) · [hackaday.com](https://hackaday.com/2016/05/09/glue-your-sumo-robot-to-the-mat-with-custom-sticky-tires/)
- **Datasheet:** [smooth-on.com/products/vytaflex-20](https://www.smooth-on.com/products/vytaflex-20/)
- **Purchase in Argentina:** see section 3 — Duoflex is the official distributor; the VF20 **is not published online today**, request direct quotation.

#### 3. Molding with Dragon Skin 10 (platinum silicone Shore 10A) — confirmed availability in Argentina

- **What it is:** platinum curing silicone. Series available in 10A / 15A / 20A / 30A.
- **Specs verified 3-0** (Smooth-On technical bulletin rev. April 2025): DS10 = Shore 10A, traction 475 psi, **elongation 1000%, tear 102 pli** (Die B, ASTM D-624) — high mechanical durability despite softness, key for a soft wheel to survive competition.
- **Honest trade-off:** in the FingerTech benchmark, the silicone performed μ=1.30 vs 1.75 of the PU. It is **the locally available option, not the one with maximum grip**.
- **Note:** Dragon Skin **FX-Pro is Shore 2A** — too soft for a wheel with 0.5–1 kg load. Buy **DS 10 or DS 20**, not FX-Pro.
- **Datasheet:** [Dragon Skin Series TB (PDF)](https://www.smooth-on.com/tb/files/DRAGON_SKIN_SERIES_TB.pdf)
- **Purchase in Argentina:** verified that Duoflex Sudamericana sells Smooth-On via MercadoLibre (confirmed listing of FX-Pro 0.90 kg ≈ $76,145 ARS — price snippet without reliable date, **re-quote**).

### Engineering criterion (NO verified source in this pass — validate in bench)

#### 4. VytaFlex 10 (urethane Shore 10A)

One step more grip than VF20 at the cost of wear and dust pickup. It is worth molding a pair of each hardness and comparing on the actual silver ramp. Datasheet: [smooth-on.com/products/vytaflex-10](https://www.smooth-on.com/products/vytaflex-10/). Same purchase channel as VF20 (Duoflex, on request).

#### 5. JSumo silicone wheels SLT20 / SLT20P (Shore 20A)

In the [comparison by JSumo itself (2015)](https://blog.jsumo.com/wheel-report-2015-our-wheels-slt20-slt20p-against-to-banebots-fingertech-wheels/) they perform slightly above FingerTech in their methodology (μ 0.75 vs 0.70 — numbers **not comparable** with the 1.75 of FingerTech, different methodologies). Data to check: [arsumo.com.ar silicone spare parts list for SLT20](https://arsumo.com.ar/productos/par-de-repuesto-silicona-para-rueda-slt20/) — there would be national stock.

#### 6. Recycled photocopier/printer rollers — original team hypothesis, NOW WITH SOURCE

**Verified 2026-07-03 against [Yamauchi](https://www.yamauchi-rubber.com/products/copiers_and_printers-paper_feed_transport_rollers/)** (standard supplier in the photocopier industry): paper feed rollers are **EPDM Shore A20–45**, specifically formulated to **retain a high coefficient of friction even with paper dust**, with a key design trick: **grooves where dust accumulates while the surface wears and self-renews**. That is: the team's hypothesis was correct in material (same hardness range as FingerTech) and also provides a transferable design idea (see "Design Guide"). Downsides remain: fixed diameter and axis, need to machine the coupling, specific hardness unknown. Good option for **zero-cost prototype**, not the final solution.

#### 7. Commercial PU wheels Shore 30A: MAXYNOS and BaneBots

- **MAXYNOS High Traction Robot Wheel** (verified 2026-07-03): PU Shore **30A** on CNC aluminum 6061 rim, **51 mm**, 6 mm axle with M4 clamp, designed for competition. **USD 13.99 per pair (tire only)** — cheaper than FingerTech. At the time of verification, it was **out of stock** ("restock coming soon"): [maxynos.net](https://maxynos.net/products/high-traction-robot-wheel-51mm-shore-a30). Robust alternative if the A20 wears out too much.
- **BaneBots (PU ~30A)**: commercial, robust, easy to obtain. In the JSumo comparison, they ranked last in grip (μ 0.55 in their test) for being harder. "Safe but mediocre" option — documented to be discarded with argument.

#### 8. Soft TPU printed in 3D (Filaflex 60A–70A or similar)

Maximum convenience if there is a direct-drive printer: iterate band design in hours. But 60A printable is much harder than 20A molded → clearly inferior grip. **Recommended use: print the rim and mold the band on top**, not as a traction surface.

#### 9. High-grip adhesive tapes as experimental tread (3M / Heskins) — NEW, verified

Industrial "gripping" tapes applied as a tread over a rigid printed wheel. Data verified against datasheet:

- **Heskins TackyGrip H3470** ([datasheet](https://www.heskins.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/H3470-TackyGrip-Data-Sheet-2019.pdf), read directly): elastomeric film 0.7 mm over PET, **SCoF dry 2.6 (angle 69°)** measured by Sotter Engineering, acrylic adhesive 25 N/25 mm, widths from 6 mm. [Product page](https://www.heskins.com/products/tackygrip).
- **3M Gripping Material (TB/GM family, micro-replicated):** for **GM400** a secondary source mirroring the TDS reports **kinetic COF 3.0 dry AND wet** @ 0.0207 MPa ([lookpolymers](https://www.lookpolymers.com/polymer_3M-GM400-Gripping-Material.php)). The TB641 can be found at [DigiKey](https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/3m/TB641-1-X15/7671438) and there is a listing on [MercadoLibre AR](https://www.mercadolibre.com.ar/3m-material-de-agarre-tb641-negro-1-in-x-15-ft/p/MLA27560760) (stock to verify).

**Serious warnings before using them in competition:** (a) the COFs are measured as static grip material (gloves, handles), not as a rolling wheel — the wear of the microstructure and dust pickup in continuous rolling are not characterized; (b) the tape seam is a failure point; (c) **if the adhesive edge is exposed, it can lift the black tape from the track = disqualification for field damage**. Recommended use: bench experiment to know the grip ceiling, with beveled/sealed edges, never as a competition wheel without passing the "does not leave a mark" criterion.

#### 10. Latex/natural rubber band over printed rim

Strips of latex camera or stretched latex tube over 3D rim, or **caramel rubber in 2–5 mm sheet** cut into bands and glued with flexible adhesive (AR suppliers of sheet: [Gomatex](https://gomatex.com.ar/categoria/goma-en-plancha), [Gomaeme](https://gomaeme.com.ar/producto/planchas-de-goma-y-otros-materiales/plancha-de-goma-caramelo/) — stock/hardness to verify; commercial caramel rubber usually ranges A35–A50). Low cost, works, but natural rubber yielded μ=1.05 in the FingerTech benchmark — it is the bottom of the list. Always test that it does not mark the track.

#### What NOT to use, with the why

- **Sorbothane** — now with numbers from the manufacturer (Data Sheet 101 official, rev. 2021, read directly): the famous "μ static 15.8 / dynamic 3.3 on polished steel" circulating comes from **MatWeb (ASTM D1894), NOT from the current official datasheet, which does not publish any COF**. And although the tack is real, its official mechanical properties disqualify it as a wheel: Sorbothane 30 Shore **00** has break traction **26 psi** and tear **12 lb/in** — 18× and 8× worse than Dragon Skin 10 (475 psi / 102 pli). It is a damper, not a tread: it tears, and its very high hysteresis (tan δ ≈ 0.7–0.8) makes it a wheel that brakes the robot itself (rolling resistance). Moreover, the verified physics (§1.2) already showed that "peel adhesion" does not translate into tangential friction. *Only legitimate use: laboratory experiment to understand the theoretical ceiling, or static grip pads.*
- **Ecoflex 00-30 / silicones Shore 00 / Dragon Skin FX-Pro (2A):** too soft — excessive deformation under load, risk of delamination of the rim, dust vacuum.
- **Sticky surface treatments** (belt dressing, spray adhesives): grip that dies in meters with dust, and leave residue — prohibited by the rule of not damaging the field ([rules 2026](https://rescue.rcj.cloud/rules/2026/RCJRescueLine2026-final.pdf)).
- **Dry gecko-type adhesives (microfibers, e.g., Setex):** real technology but for manipulation/static directional grip; in continuous rolling with dust, they lose the microstructure. Not applicable to wheels today.

## 3b. Design guide for the molded wheel

*Engineering criterion + verified industrial practice (Yamauchi, sumo casting guides). Validate in bench.*

| Parameter | Recommendation | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Elastomeric band | 2.5–4 mm thick over rigid hub | Sufficient deformation to copy the surface without massive flexing that brakes the robot |
| Hub | Rigid (aluminum, nylon, PETG, PA-CF), with **mechanical anchoring**: circumferential grooves, transverse perforations, or teeth — do not rely solely on chemical adhesion | Delaminated PU/silicone is the typical failure mode of homemade wheels |
| Profile | Slightly convex, rounded edges | Stable contact on ramp and over steps/gaps of 3 mm between tiles |
| Texture | Matte smooth, or **longitudinal/diagonal micro-striations** | Grooves provide places to deposit dust and self-renew the surface — this is the design used by Yamauchi in photocopier rollers and what Ask Aaron recommends for sticky treads |
| Large knobs | NO for Rescue Line | Catch tape, generate vibration over speed bumps |
| Chemical safety (PU casting) | Read SDS, gloves, ventilation (isocyanates), scale if mixing by weight, do not mix systems from different brands | Urethanes part B contain isocyanates — this is handled by an adult, not students |

## 4. Recommended action plan

1. **Now:** buy the **VytaFlex 30 (0.86 kg)** trial kit published on ML and mold the first set of wheels (3D printed mold). This validates the mold, process, and ramp test protocol.
2. **In parallel:** request a quote for **VF20** (and VF10 if they bring it) from Duoflex via WhatsApp. If it arrives, mold the second set and compare hardnesses on the actual ramp.
3. **In parallel:** quote import of **2 pairs of FingerTech A20 (50.8 mm)** — tested commercial plan B in competition.
4. **Non-negotiable pits protocol** with any soft compound: **clean the wheels with isopropyl alcohol before each run**. Budget IPA wipes in the kit.
5. **Mandatory bench validation** (golden rule 3), three complementary tests — record everything in [testing/TEST_LOG.md](../../testing/TEST_LOG.md):
   - **Inclined plane:** plate of the actual surface (painted MDF and silver ramp), complete robot on top, tilt until sliding → **μ = tan(angle)**. References: 25°→0.47, 35°→0.70, 45°→1.00, 55°→1.43, 60°→1.73.
   - **Horizontal pull with dynamometer** (or luggage scale): robot on the actual surface, pull horizontally until it slides, 5 repetitions → **μ = F/N** with N = weight of the robot. More repeatable than the inclined plane for comparing materials.
   - **Repeatability with dirt:** measure μ with clean wheels → 5 laps of track → measure again → 10 laps → measure. **Rejection criterion: loses >25% grip after 10 laps** or leaves residue/mark on white paper and black tape.
6. **Ask in the [official RCJ forum](https://junior.forum.robocup.org/t/wheel-recommendations-for-robocup-junior-rescue-maze/5384)** what the top Rescue Line teams use — the research found no verifiable source on this.
7. **Consult Reyfil** (WhatsApp +54 9 11 2302-2268) if they coat in Shore A20–A30 with the message from section 3 — if the answer is yes, it is the path for professional manufacturing without our own chemistry.

An independent analysis generated by ChatGPT on the same topic was reviewed. It agreed on the core (PU Shore A20–A30, FingerTech as benchmark, physics of two mechanisms, Sorbothane unsuitable as a wheel). Result of contrasting its new ideas against primary source:

**Corrected (the claim from ChatGPT was imprecise):**
